aid: $1,000 (estimated)

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
eligibility: High school students graduating in 2026, 2027, or 2028; must be at least 15 years old as of January 1 of competition year and not turn 19 before July 31 of competition year
cost: $125 per school registration fee + $5 per student (school must register first; individual cost covered by school)
aid: National Finalists receive travel and lodging for finals; no financial aid needed for earlier rounds
notes: School registration opens August 1, 2026. School registration and payment deadline is November 8, 2026. Open Exam typically early February, Semifinal Exam early March, National Finals in June. Strongly recommended for biology-focused students. Top 20 finalists get all-expenses-paid trip to National Finals at a host university (recently Purdue, Harvard).

name: AMC 10/12 (American Mathematics Competitions)
eligibility: AMC 10: students in grade 10 or below. AMC 12: students in grade 12 or below. Both: must be under 19.5 years of age on competition day.
cost: Early bird $55 (by Sept 30, 2026), Regular $75 (by Oct 15, 2026), Late $115 (by Oct 28, 2026, returning managers only)
aid: No direct financial aid; some schools cover fees
notes: Competition dates: AMC 10A/12A on November 5, 2026; AMC 10B/12B on November 13, 2026. Registration through school's competition manager. Considered the gateway to the US Math Olympiad pipeline. Top 5% on AMC 12 or top 2.5% on AMC 10 qualify for AIME.

name: AIME (American Invitational Mathematics Examination)
deadline: Invitation-only; based on AMC 10/12 performance (AMC results released ~December 2026, AIME typically held February 2027)
eligibility: Top ~2.5% of AMC 10 scorers and top ~5% of AMC 12 scorers nationally. Invitation is automatic through MAA.
cost: No additional cost beyond AMC registration for qualifiers
aid: None needed; free to qualifying students
notes: AIME I typically held in early February; AIME II in mid-February (students take whichever doesn't conflict with school schedule). AMC + AIME score determines USAMO/USAJMO qualification. Strong performance opens doors to top-tier math camps (Ross, PROMYS, SUMaC, etc.).

name: National Science Bowl (NSB) — Connecticut Regional
eligibility: High school students on teams from CT schools. Maximum 3 teams per school. Up to 5 students per team.
cost: Registration fee varies by region; typically $50-150 per team
aid: National finalists receive travel stipends to Washington, DC
notes: 2026 CT Regional was February 28, 2026 (max 42 teams). 2027 dates TBD but typically late Feb. 2027 National Finals: April 29 - May 3, 2027. CT has a dedicated regional competition. Biology questions are a major category. Good complement to other science competitions.

name: BioGENEius Challenge
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 from the United States
cost: Varies by state partner; typically minimal or no cost
aid: Finalists receive travel support and recognition at the international competition
notes: 2026 entries closed. 2027 cycle typically opens in fall 2026. Students present original research in biotechnology. International competition is held annually (2024 was in NYC at BioFuture Conference). Very strong alignment with biology research interests. Cash prizes for winners.

name: Genes in Space
eligibility: Students in grades 7-12 in the United States
aid: Winner's experiment launched to ISS; prizes include lab equipment and supplies
notes: 2026 contest closed. Next contest announced in fall 2026. Students design a PCR-based DNA experiment to solve a space exploration problem. Winning team works with scientists to prepare their experiment for launch. Excellent for biology + space/engineering crossover interests. No cost to participate.

name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
deadline: Rolling — first contest typically early December 2026
eligibility: Open to all middle and high school students worldwide (for participation). US students eligible for national team selection.
aid: Free; no financial aid needed
notes: Four contests per season: December, January, February, and March (each 3-4 days long). Each contest has 3 problems in 4-5 hours. Relevant for computational biology — programming skills increasingly valuable in bioinformatics. Free and self-paced. Also selects US team for European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics (EGOI) for top female students.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
deadline: Mid-December (typically Dec 10-15); check 2027 dates
eligibility: Rising high school seniors (entering last year); must be 16+ by July 1 of program year; US citizens and permanent residents; strong academic background in STEM
aid: Fully funded — all educational, housing, and dining expenses covered. Travel to/from MIT not covered.
notes: The most prestigious high school STEM research program in the US. 6 weeks at MIT. Co-sponsored by CEE and MIT. Applications open to 11th graders. Strong match for biology interest.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
deadline: Late January/early February (international: Jan 24; US: late Jan); check for 2027
eligibility: Current high school juniors; completed relevant coursework (e.g., chemistry for biochemistry track); ages 15-19 during program
cost: $4,300 - $9,800 (sliding scale; maximum all-inclusive fee for high-income families)
aid: Free for families with income ≤$75,000; financial aid grants meeting 100% demonstrated need available covering tuition, room, board, and travel
notes: One of the oldest and most prestigious pre-college STEM programs (since 1959). Conducted at multiple university campuses nationwide. High-income families pay max fee of ~$9,800. ~30-36 students per campus.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
deadline: Late February (typically ~Feb 22); check for 2027
eligibility: Current high school junior or senior at US high school (graduating classes of 2026 or 2027); strong academic record; US citizen or permanent resident
aid: Free to attend; minimum $500+ stipend provided (higher for underrepresented students). $40 application fee (waivers available).
notes: Highly selective (~4-5% acceptance rate). 8 weeks, full-time in Stanford Medicine labs. One of the best biomedical research programs for high schoolers. Stipend provided.

name: NIH High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
deadline: March 1 (typically); check for 2027
eligibility: High school students; must be 17+ by June of program year; US citizen or permanent resident; enrolled in high school
aid: Stipend provided; amount varies by education level. No tuition.
notes: No direct housing provided — students arrange own accommodation or commute. Extremely valuable for biomedical research experience. One of the best government science internships.

name: Simons Summer Research Program
deadline: Early February (typically Feb 1-8); check for 2027
eligibility: Current 11th graders (high school juniors); strong academic record; no prior research experience required
aid: Fully funded; students receive a stipend. No tuition or program fees.
notes: 6-week program on Stony Brook campus. Supported by Simons Foundation. Includes a research symposium at end. One of the top free STEM research programs.

name: Anson L. Clark Scholars Program
deadline: Mid-February (typically ~Feb 16); check for 2027

aid: Free tuition, room, board; $750 stipend provided; travel costs not covered
notes: One of the most prestigious fully-funded research programs. Highly selective. Strong for biology research.

name: MITES Summer (MIT Introduction to Technology, Engineering, and Science)
deadline: February 1; check for 2027
eligibility: High school juniors; US citizen or permanent resident; strong academic record; designed for students from underrepresented or underserved backgrounds
aid: Free — all educational, food, and boarding costs covered. Students only pay transportation to/from MIT.
notes: 6-week residential at MIT. Free of charge. Highly selective. Strong STEM focus. Considered a 'feeder' to top college admissions. Formerly called MITES (Minority Introduction).

name: Notre Dame Leadership Seminars
deadline: Mid-January (typically ~Jan 17); check for 2027
eligibility: Current high school juniors; academically talented; demonstrated community leadership; US citizens/permanent residents preferred
aid: Fully funded — tuition, housing, and meals paid by University of Notre Dame. Travel costs not covered.
notes: 10-day program. Does not specifically focus on biology or law but the 'Global Issues' or 'Environment' tracks could align with interests. Highly prestigious free program.

name: Brown University Summer@Brown Pre-College Program

notes: Flexible format — can take 1, 2, or more weeks. Open Curriculum allows combining interests. On-campus residential experience in Providence, RI.

name: UCLA Mock Trial Summer Institute
deadline: Rolling; typically spring; check for 2027
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12)
aid: Not typically available

name: National Student Leadership Conference (NSLC) — Law & Advocacy / Marine Biology

name: Yale Summer Session — Pre-College
